text.p: Gold prices firmed in New York with most base metals also firmer. Crude oil rose, wheat prices were mixed and sugar eased. The CRB index was up 0.17 at 234.19.
METALS - Copper made steady upside afternoon progress and ended firmly in the plus column after an early dip to five-month lows, with other metals generally following suit.
Three months copper ended at $2,280 per tonne, compared to $2,267 at Wednesday's finish. Cash/threes backwardation softened to $135/$145, about $50 narrower than the previous day.
Shortcovering helped copper recover after prices tumbled in the pre-market to a low of $2,226, a new low since February 12.
But traders said resistance in a $2,290-$2,310 band may cap the market, noting that copper turned back from a high of $2,288 during the afternoon kerb.
News that the majority of miners at the Neves Corvo copper mine had rejected a renewed company offer for implementing continuous working was mildly supportive.
Zinc surged to new highs since September 1990 early in the day, and remained strong. By the end of the kerb it was $17 firmer at $1,511.
Aluminium also crept higher with copper, although traders said it was relatively ignored compared to copper and zinc. Prices were last at $1,579, up $9.
Nickel bounced off a low of $6,705 and made its way back above $6,800 resistance. It settled $80 firmer at $6,830 at the end of the kerb.
Lead bounced up $9 to $641, while alloy was indicated a touch firmer at $1,435/1,440.

The day's worst performer was tin, which failed to recover from fund liquidation and stop-loss selling on Wednesday. It posted a fresh 2-1/3 year low of $5,420 and ended the kerb barely different at $5,440, versus $5,450 on Wednesday.
GOLD - COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended higher, led by a jump in gold prices on fund, trade house, and commission house buying, on good volume, traders said.

"Gold has been technically oversold for sometime now, and open interest on COMEX is way, way up, so a short covering rally would not be surprising," Credit Lyonnais Rouse's New York chief bullion dealer, Scott Mehlman, said.

"Today's move appeared to be triggered by breaches of minor resistance around $321.00 and then $324.00, but August gold still has to get back up through major resistance around $325.00 to set off a big rally," he said.
COMEX August gold ended up $6.00 at $324.70 an ounce, its highest level in ten days, with total COMEX gold volume estimated at 60,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $323.50/00, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $319.40 and the New York close Wednesday around $317.80/30.

GRAINS - CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed mixed as a slide in corn and soybeans trimmed early gains, especially in the nearby months, traders said. Wheat held firm most of the session on support from the export sector. USDA said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended July 10 totalled 586,900 tonnes, above expectations for 250,000 to 450,000 tonnes. CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed unchanged to six cents per bushel higher, with July unchanged at $3.25. September closed 1/4 cent higher at $3.31-3/4.

OIL - NYMEX gasoline ended sharply higher on concerns that a tropical storm could disrupt refinery operations in the U.S. Gulf when supplies of a key gasoline blending component are already tight. Gasoline pushed the rest of the oil complex higher, with August crude ending up 34 cents at $19.99 a barrel and August heating oil finishing up 1.21 cents a gallon at 53.89 cents.

SUGAR - CSCE world sugar futures ended weaker and near the bottom of the day's trading range after the market retraced gains made during the previous session. The benchmark October contract settled 0.14 cent weaker at 11.16 cents per lb, having ranged from 11.31 to 11.15 cents. Second-position March ended 0.12 cent lower at 11.35 cents, while the rest of the board finished down 0.04 to 0.04 cent.
